heading.en: Four equal bonds from unequal orbitals?

hook.en: Carbon’s *valence* orbitals are one 2s and three 2p, which are not alike. Yet all four C–H bonds in methane are identical. Mixing orbitals, hybridisation, solves the puzzle.
hook.kn: ಕಾರ್ಬನ್‌ನ ವೇಲೆನ್ಸಿ ಕಕ್ಷಕಗಳು ಒಂದು 2s ಮತ್ತು ಮೂರು 2p, ಅವು ಒಂದೇ ರೀತಿಯಲ್ಲ. ಆದರೂ ಮೀಥೇನ್‌ನ ನಾಲ್ಕು C–H ಬಂಧಗಳು ಸಮಾನ. ಕಕ್ಷಕಗಳ ಮಿಶ್ರಣ, ಅಂದರೆ ಸಂಕರೀಕರಣ, ಈ ಒಗಟನ್ನು ಬಿಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Carbon's valence orbitals are one 2 seconds and three 2p, which are not alike. Yet all four C-H bonds in methane are identical. Mixing orbitals, hybridisation, solves the puzzle. In this lesson: Explain bond formation by orbital overlap.
Distinguish sigma and pi bonds.
Identify sp, sp squared, sp cubed, sp cubedd and sp cubedd squared hybridisation.

title.en: Orbital overlap: σ and π bonds

body.en: Valence bond theory: a covalent bond forms when half-filled *orbitals* of two atoms overlap and the electrons pair with opposite spins. For H$_2$ the energy is lowest at 74 pm, and 435.8 kJ mol$^{-1}$ is released per mole of bonds. Head-on (axial) overlap gives a σ bond; sideways overlap of parallel p orbitals gives a π bond. A σ bond is stronger because the overlap is greater. A single bond is one σ; a double bond is σ + π; a triple bond is σ + 2π.
body.kn: ಅರ್ಧ ತುಂಬಿದ ಕಕ್ಷಕಗಳ ಅತಿವ್ಯಾಪನದಿಂದ ಸಹವೇಲೆನ್ಸೀಯ ಬಂಧ ರೂಪುಗೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತದೆ. ಅಕ್ಷೀಯ ಅತಿವ್ಯಾಪನ σ ಬಂಧ, ಪಾರ್ಶ್ವ ಅತಿವ್ಯಾಪನ π ಬಂಧ. σ ಬಂಧ π ಗಿಂತ ಬಲವಾದದ್ದು.

narration.en: A covalent bond forms when half-filled orbitals overlap. Head-on overlap gives a strong sigma bond, sideways overlap gives a pi bond. A double bond is one sigma and one pi; a triple bond is one sigma and two pi.

title.en: Overlap, sigma and pi bonds, and hybrid orbitals

say.en: As two hydrogen atoms approach, the energy falls to a minimum at 74 picometres, where 435.8 kilojoules per mole is released. Closer than that, the nuclei repel.
Head-on overlap gives a strong sigma bond. Side-ways overlap of two parallel p orbitals gives a weaker pi bond, above and below the axis.
Carbon has only two unpaired electrons, yet forms four equal bonds. One 2s electron is promoted, and the 2s and three 2p orbitals mix into four sp3 hybrids.
More s-character means a wider angle: sp 180 degrees with 50 percent s, sp2 120 with 33, sp3 109.5 with 25.

body.en: *Hybridisation* is the mixing of atomic orbitals of similar energy on the same atom to give an equal number of identical hybrid orbitals, which point as far apart as possible. sp: linear, 180° (BeCl$_2$, C$_2$H$_2$). sp$^2$: trigonal planar, 120° (BF$_3$, C$_2$H$_4$). sp$^3$: tetrahedral, 109.5° (CH$_4$; also NH$_3$ and H$_2$O with lone pairs). sp$^3$d: trigonal bipyramidal (PCl$_5$). sp$^3$d$^2$: octahedral (SF$_6$). Hybrid orbitals form σ bonds; unhybridised p orbitals form π bonds.
body.kn: ಸಮಾನ ಶಕ್ತಿಯ ಕಕ್ಷಕಗಳು ಮಿಶ್ರಣಗೊಂಡು ಅಷ್ಟೇ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯ ಸಮಾನ ಸಂಕರ ಕಕ್ಷಕಗಳಾಗುತ್ತವೆ. sp ರೇಖೀಯ 180°, sp² ತ್ರಿಕೋನ ಸಮತಲ 120°, sp³ ಚತುಷ್ಫಲಕ 109.5°, sp³d ತ್ರಿಕೋನ ದ್ವಿಪಿರಮಿಡ್, sp³d² ಅಷ್ಟಫಲಕ.

heading.en: VSEPR Theory, Valence Bond Theory and Hybridisation

tagline.en: Predicting shapes from electron pairs with VSEPR, how orbital overlap forms sigma and pi bonds, and the hybridisation schemes sp, sp², sp³, sp³d and sp³d².

myth.en: NH₃ has three bonds, so nitrogen is sp² hybridised and the molecule is trigonal planar.

truth.en: N in NH₃ has three bond pairs and one lone pair: four electron pairs, so it is sp³ hybridised. The electron-pair geometry is tetrahedral and the shape, which names only atom positions, is trigonal pyramidal. Learners count only bonds. Hybridisation counts every electron pair on the central atom (σ bonds + lone pairs). π bonds and atoms do not decide it.

title.en: Valence bond theory and orbital overlap

say.en: Valence bond theory (Heitler, London, Pauling) explains a bond as the overlap of half-filled atomic orbitals of opposite spin. As two H atoms approach, nucleus–electron attraction lowers the energy and nucleus–nucleus and electron–electron repulsion raise it.

Valence bond theory with plain s and p orbitals cannot explain why the four C–H bonds in CH₄ are identical and 109.5° apart. Pauling's answer is hybridisation: atomic orbitals of similar energy on the same atom mix to give an equal number of identical hybrid orbitals, which point in fixed directions and overlap better than pure orbitals.

goal.en: Predicting shapes from electron pairs with VSEPR, how orbital overlap forms sigma and pi bonds, and the hybridisation schemes sp, sp², sp³, sp³d and sp³d².

question.en: What is the shape of SF₄?

explain.en: S has 4 bond pairs and 1 lone pair (5 pairs). The lone pair takes an equatorial position of the trigonal bipyramid, leaving a see-saw shape.

task.en: Match each molecule with its shape.

explain.en: Count bond pairs and lone pairs on the central atom first; the total gives the electron geometry, and the lone pairs carve the final shape out of it.

takeaway.en: VSEPR: count all electron pairs on the central atom; lone pairs repel most and go equatorial in a trigonal bipyramid.

narration.en: Many people think: NH₃ has three bonds, so nitrogen is sp² hybridised and the molecule is trigonal planar. Actually: N in NH₃ has three bond pairs and one lone pair: four electron pairs, so it is sp³ hybridised. The electron-pair geometry is tetrahedral and the shape, which names only atom positions, is trigonal pyramidal. Learners count only bonds. Hybridisation counts every electron pair on the central atom (σ bonds + lone pairs). π bonds and atoms do not decide it.

problem.en: Count the σ and π bonds in vinylacetylene, CH₂=CH–C≡CH.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Count the σ and π bonds in vinylacetylene, CH₂=CH–C≡CH.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Count the sigma and pi bonds in vinylacetylene, CH 2=CH-C is equivalent to CH.
C-H bonds: 4, all sigma.
C=C: 1 sigma plus 1 pi; C-C: 1 sigma; C is equivalent to C: 1 sigma plus 2 pi.
Total: sigma equals 4 plus 1 plus 1 plus 1 equals 7; pi equals 1 plus 2 equals 3.
So the answer is 7 sigma and 3 pi bonds.

problem.en: State the hybridisation of each carbon in propene, CH₃–CH=CH₂.

steps.en: CH₃ carbon: four σ bonds, no π → sp³.
CH carbon: three σ bonds and one π → sp².
CH₂ carbon: three σ bonds and one π → sp².

narration.en: Let us solve this together. State the hybridisation of each carbon in propene, CH₃–CH=CH₂.

say.en: Let us solve this together. State the hybridisation of each carbon in propene, CH 3-CH=CH 2.
CH 3 carbon: four sigma bonds, no pi gives sp cubed.
CH carbon: three sigma bonds and one pi gives sp squared.
CH 2 carbon: three sigma bonds and one pi gives sp squared.
So the answer is sp cubed, sp squared, sp squared.

narration.en: Recap. A covalent bond forms by overlap of half-filled orbitals. Head-on overlap gives σ; sideways overlap gives π; σ is stronger. sp 180°, sp² 120°, sp³ 109.5°, sp³d trigonal bipyramidal, sp³d² octahedral. Hybrid orbitals form only σ bonds.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ಅರ್ಧ ತುಂಬಿದ ಕಕ್ಷಕಗಳ ಅತಿವ್ಯಾಪನದಿಂದ ಸಹವೇಲೆನ್ಸೀಯ ಬಂಧ. ಅಕ್ಷೀಯ ಅತಿವ್ಯಾಪನ σ, ಪಾರ್ಶ್ವ ಅತಿವ್ಯಾಪನ π; σ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಬಲ. sp 180°, sp² 120°, sp³ 109.5°, sp³d ತ್ರಿಕೋನ ದ್ವಿಪಿರಮಿಡ್, sp³d² ಅಷ್ಟಫಲಕ. ಸಂಕರ ಕಕ್ಷಕಗಳು σ ಬಂಧಗಳನ್ನು ಮಾತ್ರ ರಚಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

title.en: Molecular orbital theory and hydrogen bonding
title.kn: ಆಣ್ವಿಕ ಕಕ್ಷಕ ಸಿದ್ಧಾಂತ ಮತ್ತು ಹೈಡ್ರೋಜನ್ ಬಂಧ

say.en: Let us recall the key ideas. A covalent bond forms by overlap of half-filled orbitals.
say.kn: ಮುಖ್ಯ ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳೋಣ. ಅರ್ಧ ತುಂಬಿದ ಕಕ್ಷಕಗಳ ಅತಿವ್ಯಾಪನದಿಂದ ಸಹವೇಲೆನ್ಸೀಯ ಬಂಧ.

say.en: Head-on overlap gives sigma; sideways overlap gives pi; sigma is stronger.
say.kn: ಅಕ್ಷೀಯ ಅತಿವ್ಯಾಪನ sigma, ಪಾರ್ಶ್ವ ಅತಿವ್ಯಾಪನ pi; sigma ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಬಲ.

say.en: sp 180 degrees, sp squared 120 degrees, sp cubed 109.5 degrees, sp cubedd trigonal bipyramidal, sp cubedd squared octahedral.
say.kn: sp 180 degrees, sp squared 120 degrees, sp cubed 109.5 degrees, sp cubedd ತ್ರಿಕೋನ ದ್ವಿಪಿರಮಿಡ್, sp cubedd squared ಅಷ್ಟಫಲಕ.

say.en: Hybrid orbitals form only sigma bonds.
say.kn: ಸಂಕರ ಕಕ್ಷಕಗಳು sigma ಬಂಧಗಳನ್ನು ಮಾತ್ರ ರಚಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.
